title: Pool thermal grok: incident breadcrumb sketch
content:
Notes to self - quick chronology:

2025-01-10 09:12 UTC - Pager: dedicated-pool-x had 5x scale-ups then immediate scale-downs, latency spikes to 900ms P95 for hosted-generation route.
2025-01-10 09:15 UTC - Observed repeated cold-start churn: new containers coming up, warm handshake failing, and then pool autoscaler reducing target.
2025-01-10 09:22 UTC - Manual intervention: scaled pool target to stable-min=20, paused autoscaler. Latency stabilized after ~3m.

Symptoms observed:
- Capacity thrash: rapid scale-ups followed by scale-downs within 30-120s window.
- Warmup time per instance ~45-70s on A100 nodes (kernel load + model mmap).
- Autoscaler cooldown appears shorter than warmup, causing under-provisioning in steady demand bursts.
- Occasionally saw device allocation failures (NVML) during hot reattach attempts.

Commands I ran (raw outputs trimmed):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool-x --show-labels -o wide
  -> many pods in ContainerCreating, some in CrashLoopBackOff due to device plugin init timeouts.

- kubectl describe node gpu-node-17 | sed -n '1,120p'
  Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu: 8
  Allocatable memory: OK
  Events: device plugin reported timeout 2025-01-10T09:05:23Z

- kc exec -n infra autoscaler-7fd5c /bin/sh -c 'ps aux | grep autoscaler'
  -> autoscaler process healthy, logs show rapid target recalcs triggered by metric bursts.

Autoscaler config excerpt (from cluster):
- minReplicas: 4
- maxReplicas: 80
- scaleUp: stabilizationWindowSeconds: 20  # suspiciously low
- scaleDown: stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
- metrics: customPrometheus (tokens/sec, queueLength)

PromQL probes I ran (timeline around incident):
- sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (pool)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route))
- pool_warm_start_duration_seconds_bucket -- shows heavy mass in 30-80s bucket

Error snippets captured from device plugin logs:
- 2025-01-10T09:06:12Z ERROR deviceplugin: Allocate failed: nvml: device not ready
- 2025-01-10T09:06:45Z WARN kubelet: pod "serve-abc" is slow to start: CNI wait 12s, device attach 42s

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stabilization windows too aggressive relative to instance warmup. scaleUp window 20s < warmup 40-70s -> autoscaler swings up then down when short bursts end before instances finish priming.
2) Device plugin intermittently failing under burst attach load (nvml timeouts), causing pods to flake and the autoscaler to see them as unsuccessful, lowering desired replicas.
3) Scheduling churn because pods have strict nodeSelector:nvidia-a100 and limited packing, so bin-packing conflicts cause preemption/evictions during concurrent scaling.
4) Cold cache (KV cache not primed) amplifies perceived latency, triggering additional scale decisions in feedback loop.

Experiments and what I tried:
- Experiment A (2025-01-10 09:30) - increased scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120s and observed behavior for 40m. Result: thrash reduced by ~70% but time-to-service for first requests increased slightly when real demand dropped quickly.
- Experiment B - bumped minReplicas to 12 and paused downscaling for 10m during controlled traffic replay. Result: no device plugin errors observed; latency steady but cost increase obvious.
- Experiment C - changed nodeSelector to allow nvidia-a40 as fallback for non-latency-critical routes. Result: scheduler placed pods on A40s; KV cache miss rate increased but fewer device attach errors.
- Experiment D - manual pre-warm: run a bootstrap job that performs dummy inference to populate KV cache on new pods. Observed lower P95 on subsequent real requests but cold-start duration unchanged.

Repro steps (best-effort):
1) Use replay load generator to push 3x baseline RPS for 60-90s with short quiet windows.
2) Observe autoscaler behavior and check pool_warm_start_duration_seconds histograms.
3) Watch device-plugin logs for NVML allocation errors.
4) Toggle scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds between 20s and 120s to see difference.

Temporary mitigations taken:
- Increased scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120s cluster-wide for dedicated pools (rolled back on 2025-01-11 14:00 after follow-ups).
- Raised minReplicas for pool-x to 12 during office hours (manual).
- Added a probe to detect NVML allocation failures and mark node as "no-new-alloc" for 2m to reduce attach pressure.

Longer-term remediation ideas (backlog):
- Autoscaler: make warmup-aware scaling policy (explicit warmupDuration per pool) so desiredReplicas only considered stable after warmup window.
- Implement jittered scaleDown policy: avoid simultaneous downscales across similar pools to prevent cascade.
- Device plugin: collaborate with infra team to improve attach concurrency handling and add exponential backoff retries for NVML errors.
- Scheduler: relax nodeSelector (fallback tiers) and prefer soft-affinity to reduce packing bottlenecks.
- Serve runtime: add faster cold-start path that warms only lightweight KV cache to reduce critical path latency for first tokens.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the NVML failure rate correlated with simultaneous attach attempts per node? Need per-node attach-rate metric.
- Can we backfill warmupDuration from historical pool_warm_start_duration_seconds for adaptive defaults?
- Risk analysis for increasing minReplicas (cost vs reliability) - calc expected monthly delta.

Notes for follow-up meeting with infra (2025-01-12):
- Share device-plugin logs and attach-rate stats (I'll capture per-node attach counts next run).
- Propose a short experiment: warmup-aware autoscaler flag on canary pool for 2 weeks.
- Discuss hardware fallback policy for latency-sensitive routes.

Scratch commands to re-run quickly:
- kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-7fd5c --since=2h | grep -E "scaleUp|scaleDown|recalc"
- prometheus_query 'pool_warm_start_duration_seconds_bucket' --start=2025-01-10T08:30:00Z --end=2025-01-10T10:00:00Z
- ./loadgen --rps 3x --pattern burst-90s --target pool-x

Random notes to self (informal):
- "thermal" metaphor: think of pool as oven heating up. If oven thermostat (autoscaler) turns off heating too early, cake (KV cache) never sets.
- Keep a copy of device-plugin change log in ticket JIRA-5042.

Next immediate actions (priority):
1) Add per-node attach-rate metric (instrument device-plugin). Owner: Marcus. ETA 2025-01-14.
2) Run controlled canary with warmup-aware flag on pool-x (owner: me). ETA 2025-01-16.
3) Triage NVML errors with infra/driver team and test attach backoff changes (owner: Ravi). ETA 2025-01-21.

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a formal postmortem if incident recurs or costs exceed threshold.
